newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March manufacturers' shipments rise 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada March manufacturers' shipments rise 0.4 pct.

text.p: Canadian manufacturers' shipments rose 0.4 percent in March, to C$35.35 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$35.22 billion (C$35.21 billion) in February, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast shipments to rise 0.5 percent, new orders to rise 0.6 percent, unfilled orders to rise 0.8 percent and an inventory/shipment ratio of 1.29.

Statistics Canada said the Canadian manufacturing sector increased shipments at a moderate pace in February and March, following a sharp increase in January. The 0.4 percent increase in shipments came from a 2.3 rise in the automotive sector, partly offset by a 0.1 decrease in the rest of manufacturing, where a mixed pattern of increases and decreases occurred, StatsCan said.

Overall, increases were recorded in 11 of the 22 major industry groups, which accounted for 43 percent of total shipments. Shipments of motor vehicles, up 2.5 percent, were particularly strong, buoyed by strong U.S. demand, the federal agency said.
The backlog of unfilled orders, a key determinant of future shipments, edged up 0.2 percent following significant increases in the previous three months.

The March increase was driven mainly by a 1.0 percent increase in the transportation equipment industry and a 1.4 percent rise in the machinery industry, StatsCan said. The electrical and electronic industry had the largest offsetting decline, falling 1.7 percent.

The agency said increases in both shipments and inventories left the inventory-to-shipment ratio unchanged at 1.30, a level that remains close to the all-time lows observed two years ago. The largest increase in inventories was a 3.9 percent rise for the aircraft and parts industry.
The most significant decline in inventories was a 0.9 percent fall in the paper and allied products industry, StatsCan said.
